source.pages: Accuracy Specifications printed pp. 20-22; Rotary Switch pp. 6-7; Measurements pp. 8-14
source.cite: Fluke 101 Users Manual, Accuracy Specifications, pp. 20 and 22 (limits computed from the published 1-year accuracy; the manual has no performance-verification table)
source.limits: Computed from the manufacturer's published 1-year accuracy specification at 90 % of each range (no 2:1 test margin)
source.report_note: The Fluke 101 Users Manual has no calibration procedure. Test points: one per range at 90 % of the range (AC volts and AC millivolts at 60 Hz and 400 Hz). Limits are the manufacturer's published 1-year accuracy specification (Users Manual pp. 20 and 22), +/-(% of reading + counts), rounded inward to the display step.
source.note: The Fluke 101 Users Manual has no performance-verification table. The 90 % test points were chosen by the lab owner; the limits are the published 1-year accuracy specification applied to each point (p. 20, p. 22). The meter has no current function. The Fluke 5522A or 5560A drives every point (or you set the calibrator by hand). High-voltage points go straight to the test value.

steps.tol_text: Specification p. 20: 1.620 to 1.980 V at 90 % of range   (±(10 % of reading), resolution 0.001 V; limits rounded inward to the display step)
steps.note: Turn the dial to Ω, then push the YELLOW button twice to activate the diode test mode (Test Diodes, p. 12). The meter shows the voltage across the diode test input; the calibrator applies 1.8 V DC.

steps.tol_text: Specification p. 22: 44.05 to 45.95 nF at 90 % of range   (±(2 % of reading + 5 counts), resolution 0.01 nF; limits rounded inward to the display step)
steps.note: Let the reading stabilize (up to 18 seconds, p. 12). The specification does not include test lead capacitance or the capacitance floor (up to 1.5 nF on the 50 nF range, p. 22 note 1): null the leads as you would on the bench if the lab practice does so (UNVERIFIED: the manual describes no REL step).
